newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Russia's Yukos to raise stake in Bulgarian bank.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Yukos to raise stake in Bulgarian bank.

text.p: Russia's second largest oil producer Yukos is expected to acquire a majority stake in Bulgaria's St Nikola International Orthodox Bank (IOB) next year, a bank official said on Monday.

"Yukos Petroleum Bulgaria will be licensed for the deal by the central bank after presenting a two-year balance sheet early next year," IOB board chairman Tsvetan Nachev told reporters after the bank's annual meeting of shareholders.
The company's Bulgarian branch, Yukos Petroleum Bulgaria, was set up in 1994 and is a major supplier of Bulgaria's biggest refinery Neftochim.
Bank sources said recently that Yukos, which now holds five percent in IOB, is expected to raise its stake to 60 percent.

The Orthodox Bank was set up some three years ago by the Bulgarian, Russian and Serbian patriarchy, the Armenian Church, Private Agricultural Investment Bank and Touristsport Bank. Both banks are now placed in receivership.
IOB's shareholders include some 150 orthodox monasteries and churches. The shareholders' meeting decided to boost the bank's capital to eight billion levs from its current two billion levs.
